newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Investors shouldn't see Asia as bloc - fund manager.
newsitem.headline: Investors shouldn't see Asia as bloc - fund manager.

text.p: Recent disparate market performances in Asia show that investors must pay more attention to individual countries rather than treating the region as a bloc, fund manager Guinness Flight Asia said on Thursday.

"Investment in the region has become more sophisticated," managing director Royce Brennan said. "The key to investing in Asia now is to view it as individual countries each moving at their own pace, rather than see it as an investment bloc whose stock markets move up and down in tandem."
Hong Kong stocks will continue to outshine the rest of the region, but there are a few bright spots that could offer promising returns in the short-term, investment director Nerissa Lee said.
"It's all relative," she said. "But for institutional money being invested in Asia, (Hong Kong) is where you want to be."

Guinness Flight is heavily overweight in Hong Kong and in China and mildly positive on Malaysia where macroeconomic concerns have been discounted while earnings growth is positive compared to Singapore and Thailand.
"The macroeconomic and trade figures seem to be better," Lee told reporters after releasing the fund management company's Asian quarterly outlook.
Guinness Flight is also building positions in Indian and South Korean stocks, albeit to a neutral holding.
In India, valuations are considered to be at the bottom of their range and market sentiment is likely to improve as real interest rates fall from punishingly high levels.

In South Korea, improved cyclical and valuation features are attracting attention even though "the current account deficit problem looks increasingly structural in nature and attempts to deregulate the economy are not convincing."
Guinness Flight remains bearish on Singapore, Thailand, Indonesia and Taiwan.

Growing disillusionment with Thailand's structural problems may lead to the market being downgraded by international investors despite signs of cyclical improvements in the economy and an improved political outlook, Guinness Flight said.

The fund company remains underweight in Indonesia, where political risk outweighs strong economic fundamentals, and questions valuation and earnings growth in Taiwan, whose economy is "bumping along the bottom of the cycle."

Guinness Flight retains a marginally underweight position in Singapore, where earnings growth remains a concern despite signs that an upturn in the electronics cycle could start to filter through next year.
Guinness Flight said it is important to put the recent weakness in Asian regional markets into context.
"It is currently fashionable among international fund managers to write the obituary for the Asian growth story due to a slowdown in economies in the region," Brennan said.
"While it is true that some stock markets are overvalued, it should be put in context. Even the most sluggish economy in the region is growing much faster than the best of the G7 economies."
